Class BalpAuditEvent

java.lang.Object
org.hl7.fhir.r4.model.Base
org.hl7.fhir.r4.model.BaseResource
org.hl7.fhir.r4.model.Resource
org.hl7.fhir.r4.model.DomainResource
org.hl7.fhir.r4.model.AuditEvent
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.support.audit.model.BalpAuditEvent
All Implemented Interfaces:
IElement, Serializable, IAnyResource, IBase, IBaseHasExtensions, IBaseHasModifierExtensions, IBaseResource, IDomainResource, SelfInitializing
Direct Known Subclasses:
CreateAuditEvent, DeleteAuditEvent, ExportAuditEvent, ImportAuditEvent, ProvideBundleRecipientAuditEvent, ProvideBundleSourceAuditEvent, QueryAuditEvent, ReadAuditEvent, UpdateAuditEvent
public abstract class BalpAuditEvent extends AuditEvent implements SelfInitializing
Base class of the AuditEvents built along the conventions of IHE BALP: the agent slices for the client and the server of a transaction, the user agent of the access token it carried, the audit source, and the entities for the patient, the data and the query. Each of those is a concept the BALP StructureDefinitions share; what differs between the patterns is which code a slice is fixed to, and that is what a subclass declares.

A subclass exposes the concepts under the names its own profile uses -- setClient / setServer for the RESTful patterns, setSource / setRecipient for the privacy disclosure ones -- and builds them with the add… methods here, so that a record populated by hand and one populated from an AuditMessage come out the same.

Every pattern is SelfInitializing: it can convert an ATNA audit record of its own shape into itself. That conversion runs the same way for all of them, so initialize(AuditMessage) is final here and a pattern contributes what is specific about it by overriding initializeFrom(AuditMessage, ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode) -- which is not defaulted to a no-op by accident: initialize is called instead of the generic AuditMessage-to-AuditEvent translation, so a pattern that added nothing of its own would emit a record without the interaction subtype, the data entity or the patient its profile requires.

Since:
5.3
Author:
Christian Ohr

    • initialize

      public final void initialize(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Converts an ATNA audit record into this pattern: the transaction subtype the record names, and then everything else through initializeFrom(AuditMessage, ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode).

      This is the same for every pattern, which is why it is fixed here. A pattern says what is specific about it by overriding initializeFrom -- and, if, which end of the transaction it records does not follow from the audit message, localRole(AuditMessage).

      Specified by:
      initialize in interface SelfInitializing
      Parameters:
      auditMessage - the audit message of the transaction being audited

    • localRole

      protected ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode localRole(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Which end of the transaction recorded this event, and therefore which agent the audit source has to mirror -- BALP states that as the val-audit-source invariant on the local actor's slice.

      For the RESTful patterns it follows from the audit message: the end that recorded it is the client or the server of the transaction. The privacy disclosure patterns fix it instead, being by definition the record of one particular side of the disclosure.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - the audit message of the transaction being audited
      Returns:
      the participant standing for the actor that recorded the event

    • initializeFrom

      protected void initializeFrom(AuditMessage auditMessage, ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode localRole)
      Fills in everything every BALP pattern takes from the audit record the same way: when the event happened, the client and server agents, the user agents, the audit source, and the entity carrying the request id that correlates the two ends of the transaction.

      What it deliberately leaves to the pattern is the part the profile fixes differently: the RESTful interaction subtype next to the transaction subtype, the entity for the data the transaction acted on, and the patient. A pattern overrides this, calls super, and adds those around it.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - the audit message of the transaction being audited
      localRole - which end of the transaction recorded it, see localRole(AuditMessage)

    • setClientAndServer

      public BalpAuditEvent setClientAndServer(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Adds the client and the server agent, taken from the active participants of an ATNA audit record. Which type each slice carries is this profile's business (clientAgentType(), serverAgentType()); where to find the participants is not, because the client of a transaction is always recorded as the ATNA source and the server as the ATNA destination.

      Either participant may be missing: an audit dataset is not guaranteed to know both ends of the transaction, and an audit record without one of the agents is still better than none at all.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - audit message to take the participants from
      Returns:
      this instance

    • addUserAgents

      public BalpAuditEvent addUserAgents(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Adds the user agent, and where applicable the OAuth client agent, of the access token the audited request carried. The transaction profiles allow both next to the client and the server.

      When the audit message carries the token's claims, they are mapped directly. That is the whole point of keeping them: the ATNA participants the claims were encoded into cannot be decoded unambiguously, because the subject organization and the client id are tagged with the same code system and are told apart only by a piece of original text. Audit messages built elsewhere carry no claims, and fall back to reading the participants.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - audit message of the transaction being audited
      Returns:
      this instance

    • setAuditSource

      public BalpAuditEvent setAuditSource(AuditMessage auditMessage, ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode localRole)
      Sets the audit source, i.e. what BALP calls the identity of the source detecting the event.

      The transaction profiles do not leave the observer free: an invariant on the agent slice of the end that wrote the record -- val-audit-source, "the Audit Source is this agent too" -- requires source.observer to be that very agent. So the observer is named after the local participant, exactly as setClientAndServer(AuditMessage) names the agent, and the two references come out identical.

      The audit source id of the ATNA record is the fallback for an audit message that does not name the local participant, since the profiles require an observer either way. It cannot be the primary: it identifies the application writing the record rather than its end of the transaction, so using it would break the invariant for every deployment that configures one.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - audit message of the transaction being audited
      localRole - which end of the transaction the audit source is
      Returns:
      this instance

    • addPatientEntityIfPresent

      protected void addPatientEntityIfPresent(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Adds the patient entity if the audit message names a patient, and does nothing otherwise.

      This is for the profiles whose patient entity is optional -- both PDQm transactions, for instance, derive from the plain query pattern but say the patient entity "SHOULD be used when one patient is explicitly identified in the query parameters". Where the entity is mandatory instead, use addRequiredPatientEntity(AuditMessage).

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - the audit message of the transaction being audited

    • addRequiredPatientEntity

      protected void addRequiredPatientEntity(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      Adds the patient entity that the Patient* variant of every BALP pattern requires, recording the patient as explicitly unknown when the audit message names none.

      Some transactions cannot always name a patient even though their profile insists on one -- Retrieve Document [ITI-68] never can, as it downloads a binary from a URL. Rather than drop such a record to a weaker profile, it keeps the profile of its transaction and marks the reference absent with the FHIR data-absent-reason extension, which is the standard way of saying that a required value is expected to exist but is not known. The record then still validates against the profile the transaction prescribes, and says plainly that the patient could not be determined.

      Parameters:
      auditMessage - the audit message of the transaction being audited
